smart-clean.title: Smart Clean
smart-clean.summary: One scan groups caches, logs, app leftovers, developer junk and old downloads into clear categories — Safe items preselected, everything else waits for you.

storage.title: Storage Explorer
storage.summary: See what’s really using your disk — Applications, Documents, Photos, Videos, Downloads, Cache and System Data — measured from your actual folders.

large-files.title: Large File Finder
large-files.summary: Surface files over 500 MB, 1 GB, 5 GB or 10 GB. Filter by type, sort by size or age, preview with Quick Look.

downloads.title: Downloads Review
downloads.summary: Old installers, disk images and archives, grouped by age — from today to older than 90 days. Nothing is ever preselected.

duplicates.title: Duplicate Finder
duplicates.summary: Exact copies confirmed with a full-content SHA-256 checksum. Keep the newest or oldest — at least one copy always stays.

apps.title: App Cleanup
apps.summary: See an app’s full footprint — caches, logs, support files, preferences — then clean its data or uninstall it. Apple apps are protected.

system-junk.title: System & Developer Junk
system-junk.summary: Clear caches and logs that rebuild themselves, plus Xcode, simulator, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Gradle and CocoaPods caches.

schedule.title: Scheduled Cleanup
schedule.summary: Daily, weekly or monthly background checks that remind you when there’s something worth cleaning — or, with your consent, clear developer caches.

cpu.title: CPU Monitoring
cpu.summary: Live CPU usage with a 60-second graph, split into user, system and idle time.

memory.title: Memory Usage
memory.summary: Used and available RAM, memory pressure, compressed memory and swap — explained in plain language.

running-apps.title: Running Apps
running-apps.summary: See which apps use the most memory and CPU, and how long each has been running.

battery.title: Battery Health
battery.summary: Charge, cycle count, maximum capacity and condition, as reported by macOS. MacBooks only.

mac-info.title: Mac Information
mac-info.summary: Model, chip, cores, GPU, memory, displays and uptime in one place.

storage-status.title: Storage Status
storage-status.summary: Used, available and potentially recoverable space, one click from the cleaner.

macos.title: macOS Information
macos.summary: Version, build and whether macOS’s own update check found an update — with a shortcut to Software Update.

smart-clean.title: One scan. Clear categories. Your call.
smart-clean.body: Smart Clean checks your caches, logs, app leftovers, developer tools and Downloads in one pass, then sorts everything into six plain-language groups. Each item says why it exists and what happens if you remove it.
points: System Junk, Browser Caches, App Leftovers, Logs & Crash Reports, Developer Junk and Old Downloads
Safe items start selected; Review items and your own files never do
Expand any group to see — and untick — every single item
smart-clean.alt: Smart Clean results grouped into System Junk, Browser Caches, App Leftovers, Logs, Developer Junk and Old Downloads

storage.title: Know where your space went.
storage.body: MacBook Cleaner measures your real folders and draws them as one storage ring. Sizes use decimal gigabytes, the same way macOS reports storage, and space that can’t be attributed to a folder is labeled honestly as System Data.
points: Applications, Documents, Photos, Videos, Downloads, Cache, Other and System Data
App-managed libraries like Photos are sized as a whole, never picked apart
Free space is read the same way macOS’s own Storage settings read it
storage.alt: Storage screen showing a colored ring broken down by category

large-files.title: Find the forgotten gigabytes.
large-files.body: Old screen recordings, virtual machine images, installers you meant to delete. Large File Finder looks through Downloads, Desktop, Documents and Movies and lists the biggest files first.
points: Size thresholds: 500 MB, 1 GB, 5 GB and 10 GB
Filter by videos, disk images, archives, installers or documents
Quick Look and Reveal in Finder before you decide
large-files.alt: Large Files list filtered to files over 500 MB

downloads.title: A Downloads folder you can actually read.
downloads.body: Downloads are grouped by age — Today, This Week, This Month, older than 30 days and older than 90 days — with quick views for installers and disk images, archives, duplicate downloads and large downloads.
points: Installers and disk images you’ve already used are easy to spot
These are your files: nothing in Downloads is ever preselected
Every removal asks for confirmation
downloads.alt: Downloads screen with files grouped by age

duplicates.title: Same file, three times? Keep one.
duplicates.body: Duplicates in Downloads, Desktop, Documents and Movies are matched by exact size, narrowed with a quick fingerprint, then confirmed by hashing the full contents — so “looks similar” never counts as a duplicate.
points: Keep newest or keep oldest across every set in one click
You can never select every copy of a file — one always stays
All checks run on your Mac
duplicates.alt: Duplicate files grouped into sets with wasted space per set

apps.title: Uninstall apps — and what they leave behind.
apps.body: Pick an app to see its real footprint: the app bundle plus its caches, logs, application support files, preferences, containers, saved state and web data. Clean just the data, or move the whole app to the Trash.
points: Sort apps by size, name or least recently used
Apple’s own apps — and MacBook Cleaner itself — can’t be uninstalled
Only apps in /Applications or ~/Applications are accepted
apps.alt: App Cleanup showing an app’s caches, logs and preferences

system-junk.title: Caches that rebuild themselves. Gone.
system-junk.body: System Junk lists app caches and logs from your Library, split into Safe to Clean and Review Recommended. Turn on Developer Cleanup to include heavy build and package caches.
points: Xcode DerivedData, Archives, iOS & watchOS Device Support, Simulator caches and devices
npm, Yarn, pnpm, Gradle, CocoaPods caches and Android emulator images
Each item explains what rebuilding it will cost you
system-junk.alt: System Junk screen with Safe to Clean and Review Recommended sections

schedule.title: Stay tidy without thinking about it.
schedule.body: Choose daily, weekly or monthly and a time of day. MacBook Cleaner checks quietly in the background — no window opens — and either reminds you, or cleans a fixed list of developer caches if you’ve explicitly allowed it.
points: Remind me: a notification when there’s enough to clean or space is running low
Clean automatically: only six developer caches, at least 1 GB, capped at 10 GB and 50 items per run
Documents, Photos, Videos, Desktop and personal folders are never removed automatically
schedule.alt: Scheduled Cleanup settings with frequency, mode and eligible categories

performance.title: Your Mac at a glance — live.
performance.body: The Performance tab shows CPU, memory, storage and battery in one dashboard, with live 60-second graphs and a plain-language Mac Health summary. Every status comes straight from macOS; there’s no made-up “health score”.
points: Live CPU usage split into user, system and idle time
Memory used, available, compressed and swap — plus macOS’s own memory pressure
Updates every few seconds while you’re looking, and pauses completely when you’re not
performance.alt: Performance dashboard with CPU, memory, storage and battery gauges and a Mac Health summary

running-apps.title: See what’s using your memory and CPU.
running-apps.body: Running Apps lists the apps in your Dock with their CPU use, memory and how long they’ve been running. Helper processes are counted with their app, so a browser’s many tabs add up to one honest number.
points: Sort by CPU, memory, running time or name
Switch between apps, background processes or everything
Click any app for details: launch time, threads, process ID and location
running-apps.alt: Running Apps list sorted by memory with CPU and running time

battery.title: Understand your battery.
battery.body: On MacBooks, see the charge, cycle count, maximum capacity, power source and condition — the same values System Settings uses. On desktop Macs, the battery section simply doesn’t appear.
points: Cycle count, with the design cycle count when the battery reports one
Maximum capacity and condition exactly as macOS reports them
Information only — no app can repair or restore a battery
battery.alt: Battery Health screen showing charge, maximum capacity and cycle count

mac-info.title: Everything important about your Mac.
mac-info.body: Model, chip, CPU and GPU cores, memory, storage, displays, macOS version and build, and how long your Mac has been running — collected once and shown in one tidy place.
points: macOS update status from macOS’s own automatic check, with a shortcut to Software Update
Your serial number is never read
All of it stays on your Mac
mac-info.alt: Mac Info screen listing hardware details and macOS version

page.intro: MacBook Cleaner combines a storage analyzer, large-file and duplicate finders, an app uninstaller and a cache cleaner with a Mac performance monitor — CPU, memory, running apps, battery health and Mac information — all processed locally on your Mac.
page.monitorIntro: Live CPU and memory, the apps using the most resources, battery health and everything important about your Mac — read locally from macOS, refreshed only while you’re looking.
page.notDoingIntro: Plenty of “cleaner” apps promise everything. Here’s what this one deliberately leaves out.
page.ctaTitle: Ready to see what’s taking up space?

extras.title: Scan exclusions
extras.body: Add files or folders that should never be suggested — manually or on a schedule.

extras.title: Confirm before cleanup
extras.body: On by default. Turn it off to skip the dialog for Safe-only cleanups; Review items and your own files always ask.

extras.title: Developer cleanup toggle
extras.body: Hide Xcode, simulator and package-manager caches entirely if you don’t need them.

extras.title: Light, dark or system
extras.body: Follows your Mac’s appearance, or pick one.

extras.title: Native notifications
extras.body: Scheduled-cleanup reminders and summaries, using macOS notifications.

extras.title: Trash overview
extras.body: See how much space the Trash is using and open it in Finder when you’re ready to empty it.

extras.title: Reset all data
extras.body: Clear settings, exclusions, schedule and history in one step. Never touches your files.

notDoing: No RAM “boosting” — Performance shows memory use, it doesn’t fiddle with it
No speed-up promises or startup-item tweaks
No permanent deletion or file shredding
No cleaning of system folders outside your home folder
